How to use Ventoy to boot multiple OS ISOs from one USB drive
recent_posts.summary: Ventoy is a free, open-source tool that lets you store multiple ISO images on a single USB drive and boot from any of them without reformatting. Instead of using Rufus or Etcher to flash one OS per drive, you simply copy ISO files to the Ventoy-formatted drive and select which OS to install at boot. The walkthrough covers downloading and installing Ventoy on Windows, copying Linux and Windows ISOs, booting into the menu, and resolving Secure Boot issues by enrolling keys from disk.

recent_posts.title: Privacy browser comparison for daily use and anonymous browsing
recent_posts.summary: A practical comparison of privacy-focused browsers versus mainstream options like Chrome, Edge, Safari, and Firefox. Using real UK news websites as test cases, the video demonstrates how ad-heavy and tracking-heavy mainstream browsers are compared to privacy alternatives. Recommended browsers for daily use include Brave and Mullvad Browser (based on Firefox/Tor), with LibreWolf as another Firefox-based option. For anonymous browsing, Tor Browser is recommended. Resources like privacyguides.org and privacytests.org are highlighted for independent verification. Opera is flagged for Chinese ownership concerns, and DuckDuckGo browser gets a mixed review.

recent_posts.title: Cisco unveils quantum switch to network multiple quantum computers
recent_posts.summary: Cisco Quantum Labs has unveiled a universal quantum switch that routes quantum information via single photons through standard optical fiber without measuring or destroying the quantum state. The device is fully reconfigurable and non-blocking, enabling multiple quantum computers from different vendors to be networked together into a scalable fabric — analogous to how thousands of GPUs are clustered for AI workloads. The broader implication highlighted is that once quantum computing matures, current asymmetric encryption standards like RSA will be rendered obsolete.

recent_posts.title: Speed test pulse gadget for Wi-Fi and wired network testing
recent_posts.summary: A product showcase of the 'Speed Test Pulse', a Wi-Fi and network testing gadget that can actively test Wi-Fi, wired networks, and internet backhaul connectivity. It features two modes: active spot testing and a continuous pulse mode for ongoing monitoring to detect intermittent issues. Beyond speed tests, it provides telemetry on Wi-Fi coverage, channel interference, and wired network diagnostics.

recent_posts.title: How to track dark ships using OSINT (with demos)
recent_posts.summary: An in-depth conversation with OSINT analyst Ray Baker on tracking dark fleets and shadow fleets — vessels that evade sanctions by manipulating AIS signals, changing flags, renaming ships, and going dark. The discussion covers free and paid tools like MarineTraffic and Aquacus for vessel tracking, how to investigate ship ownership through company registrations and sanctions databases, and the cybersecurity risks posed by port infrastructure including Chinese-made cranes with poor security. Also touches on drug trafficking via sea, China's maritime militia, and how AI can assist (and mislead) intelligence analysts.

recent_posts.title: Why encrypted DNS alone does not hide your browsing from ISPs
recent_posts.summary: Encrypted DNS (DoH, DoT, DoQ) does not fully protect your privacy from ISPs and network observers. Even with encrypted DNS enabled in Chrome or Firefox, the TLS Client Hello message exposes the Server Name Indication (SNI) field in plaintext, revealing which domains you visit. Using Wireshark with a network tap, this is demonstrated live against major sites like Nvidia, Microsoft, Cisco, and ChatGPT. Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) via Cloudflare can mask SNI for some sites, but many popular sites don't implement it, and even ECH-protected sites can leak domain info through third-party requests. IP address visibility is another residual leak even when SNI is hidden. Only a VPN (demonstrated with ProtonVPN/WireGuard) fully hides domain and traffic information from network observers. The post also covers UK ISP data retention laws and the trade-offs of encrypted DNS in enterprise environments.

recent_posts.title: How AI is reshaping cybersecurity offense and defense in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A conversation between David Bombal and security consultant Daniel exploring how AI is transforming both offensive and defensive cybersecurity. Attackers are using AI to scale phishing campaigns, automate recon, and run modular attack pipelines autonomously. The core argument: defenders must match attacker AI capability, not just add headcount. Daniel demos Pi (Personal AI Infrastructure), an open-source Claude Code-based agentic platform that centralizes personal context, skills, and automation — including browser automation, OSINT, red team tools, and content publishing. The discussion covers AI's societal impact on employment, privacy risks of always-on AI assistants, the danger of corporate manipulation through AI agents, and the case for local model deployments. Daniel argues AI should empower individuals, not just corporations, and that the coming disruption — while painful — could lead to more autonomous, purpose-driven work.

recent_posts.title: Windows Active Directory privilege escalation via ADCS certificate abuse
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on demo walkthrough of hacking Windows Active Directory in under 10 minutes using a chain of misconfigurations. Starting from a compromised low-privilege user (Susie), the attacker uses tools like Adeleig and Net Tools to find insecure ACL permissions, then Locksmith and Certify to identify and abuse Active Directory Certificate Services (ADCS) vulnerabilities (ESC4 → ESC1). By modifying a certificate template to allow subject alternative name enrollment, the attacker impersonates a domain admin, uses Rubeus to request a Kerberos ticket, and gains full domain controller access via PS Remoting. The demo also covers detection evasion, blue team remediation advice, career paths into pentesting (PNPT, CRTO certifications), and the continued prevalence of on-prem AD in enterprise environments.
